findings.Quote: and the look said don't, and it said I'm sorry, and it said a third thing the band had been building a wall against for four years, and there wasn't time to read it
findings.Note: Triple-anaphora 'the look said' plus the vague 'third thing' undercuts the payoff the beat is supposed to deliver; withholding the content entirely reads as coy rather than earned, weakening the four-years-suppressed-feeling payoff.
findings.Fix: Name the third thing, even obliquely, rather than gesturing at it as unspeakable.

findings.Quote: and Faith loved him a little for that — the small mercy of not ma
findings.Note: Tells the emotional payoff directly ('loved him a little') rather than letting the restrained listening carry it, undercutting the beat's stated purpose of showing grief/relief without release.
findings.Fix: Cut the naming of the emotion; let the withheld question stand alone as the mercy.

findings.Quote: She wasn't reading the room. She was reading the men who weren't in it yet.
findings.Note: aphoristic capper that states the beat's thesis directly rather than letting the preceding action carry it — reads as the author explaining the point
findings.Fix: cut the line and trust the demonstrated turns/steering to make the point, or fold it into Ethan's more concrete internal reaction

findings.Quote: his hands, when he looked at them, weren't quite his yet
findings.Note: stock post-performance depersonalization image, worn from overuse in music/performance scenes
findings.Fix: replace with a more specific physical detail unique to Ethan

findings.Quote: the engine still running with no road left to put it on
findings.Note: purple metaphor that doesn't quite parse literally — an engine with no road isn't a coherent image of adrenaline crash
findings.Fix: cut or replace with a cleaner physical description of the crash

findings.Quote: That was the thing he'd remember
findings.Note: Flash-forward narrator intrusion ('the thing he'd remember') briefly breaks the tight present-tense immersion the beat otherwise earns, a small telling-not-showing flag.
findings.Fix: Cut the framing clause and let the image of the hovering hands stand alone.

findings.Quote: It was just quiet, and it was aimed, and it had her name where a name would go.
findings.Note: Echoes the same withheld-content device as the 'third thing' in ref 0 ('a third thing...there wasn't time to read it' / 'It didn't have words on it either'); the repeated evasive gesture toward an unnamed emotional truth across both beats risks feeling like a tic rather than a deliberate motif.
findings.Fix: Either commit to naming the feeling here (since this beat is the fuller reveal) or vary the phrasing so it doesn't mirror ref 0's evasion beat-for-beat.

findings.Quote: the honest little strip telling its one truth
findings.Note: Cute personification of a light-strip that doesn't clarify what the 'truth' is; reads as filler poeticism rather than concrete image.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a concrete physical detail (steadiness of her arm, etc.).

findings.Quote: He caught the silence the way he'd once have caught a crowd going wrong under the lights — not a sound, but the absence of the sound that should have been there.
findings.Note: The stage-sense analogy is used twice in this beat (sightlines, then crowd-silence); the repetition dilutes rather than reinforces, and 'absence of the sound that should have been there' is a slightly padded restatement of the same idea already conveyed by 'she went still.'
findings.Fix: Cut one of the two stage-craft analogies to avoid redundancy.

findings.Quote: You can't talk to a picture. There's no door in him. There's just the reel.
findings.Note: The 'door' metaphor is reused from the words/door framing a sentence earlier, and 'reel' as a third image stacks metaphors past the point of clarity, slightly diluting the sharp practical distinction the beat needs.
findings.Fix: Trim to one governing image (either door or reel, not both) for cleaner contrast.

findings.Quote: relief so hard it nearly took his knees
findings.Note: Borders on cliché physical shorthand for relief.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more specific, non-generic physical tell.

findings.Quote: For one long eternity his face was down at her level
findings.Note: Stock intensifier phrase ('long eternity') undercuts the otherwise concrete tension.
findings.Fix: Cut 'long eternity' and specify a beat count or physical detail instead.

findings.Quote: she held it the way she held the last note of the slow one
findings.Note: Metaphor gestures at character backstory but is vague enough to read as authorial flourish rather than grounded recall.
findings.Fix: Anchor with one concrete sensory detail of the note/performance to earn the comparison.

findings.Quote: she'd heard the man's bad shoes
findings.Note: the callback metaphor is unclear/undercooked as presented in isolation — 'heard' paired with 'shoes' reads as a mixed-sense image without enough context to land cleanly
findings.Fix: clarify the sensory logic or cut the comparison

findings.Quote: Two people wanting the same lie didn't make it hold.
findings.Note: aphoristic, slightly pseudo-profound summary line that tells the reader the meaning instead of letting the scene's action carry it
findings.Fix: cut or integrate more concretely into her internal reasoning

findings.Quote: Ethan's heart finally did the thing
findings.Note: vague heartbeat-cliche setup, withholding for effect but generic in phrasing
findings.Fix: specify the physical sensation directly instead of the coy 'the thing'

findings.Quote: a man pouring himself through a slot the world had cut a size too small
findings.Note: strained metaphor that doesn't hold up to literal scrutiny — people don't 'pour' through slots, and the personified 'world' cutting the slot muddies the image
findings.Fix: simplify to a concrete physical description of the squeeze through the window

findings.Quote: The breach came through the wall behind them like a cough.
findings.Note: the simile is a mild reach that trades clarity for a poetic beat
findings.Fix: consider a more literal sound description

findings.Quote: She'd feel bad about using it later, from somewhere that wasn't here.
findings.Note: vague, abstracted phrasing that tells the emotional stakes rather than showing them; 'from somewhere that wasn't here' is a purple dodge
findings.Fix: Cut or ground it concretely: 'She'd feel bad about this later. Not now.'

findings.Quote: the small decisive pull of a shared secret
findings.Note: stock abstraction dressing up a simple physical action
findings.Fix: replace with a more physical, specific beat

findings.Quote: Her heartbeat picked up. She set it down again, hard.
findings.Note: heartbeat-as-fear-marker is a stock shorthand, though the second sentence attempts a fresher spin
findings.Fix: replace the heartbeat notation with a more specific physical tell

findings.Quote: the good thing, the two of them in the small lit box of the room
findings.Note: vague intensifier ('the good thing') tells the reader how to feel rather than rendering the feeling
findings.Fix: cut the label and let the preceding image carry the warmth

findings.Quote: forty-odd years worn like they'd cost him nothing
findings.Note: vague aphoristic phrasing that tells rather than shows what 'worn like nothing' looks like on him
findings.Fix: specify the concrete detail that conveys this (posture, skin, ease of movement)

findings.Quote: He and Mona had this the way two people who trust each other have it
findings.Note: circular filler line — defines trust by restating the word, adds nothing concrete
findings.Fix: cut or replace with a specific behavioral beat demonstrating the trust

findings.Quote: if he stopped he'd feel every one of his thirty-six years land at once
findings.Note: telling-not-showing fatigue via a vague aphoristic claim rather than concrete sensation
findings.Fix: ground it in one specific bodily complaint instead of an abstract age-tally

findings.Quote: Offstage he had the manner of a man politely waiting for a train
findings.Note: serviceable but slightly stock deadpan-character simile
findings.Fix: sharpen with a more idiosyncratic comparison
